author: andrewjbaker

sections.description:
Attackers do not choose targets. Automated scanners probe every WordPress site for flaws published hours earlier. CloudScale Cyber & DevTools puts the layers banks rely on in front of your site, free. It stops the attack, tells you in plain language what is wrong, and gives you the exact steps to fix it.

Why your site needs this now

  • Most WordPress vulnerabilities are in plugins and themes, so a site is only as safe as its least maintained plugin.
  • New exploits arrive within hours of a flaw being published, and AI makes them cheaper and faster to write. Your defence uses AI too.
  • A hacked site can be blacklisted by search engines, used to send spam or used to steal visitors’ data. Cleaning up costs far more than preventing it.

Stop attacks before they do damage

  • Request Firewall: 21 rules against SQL injection, cross-site scripting and code execution, before WordPress handles requests.
  • Virtual Patching: narrow, signed rules that block a published flaw in a plugin or theme you have installed until you update. Each patch is approved by a person, and is a description, never code.
  • CVE Shields: close a vulnerable plugin’s anonymous endpoints until the fixed version is installed, then lift themselves.
  • IP Reputation, Rate Limiting and Country Blocking shut out known bad traffic and floods.
  • Fake Crawler Check: proves that a visitor claiming to be Googlebot or Bingbot really is, with no delay for visitors.
  • Content Security Policy: start in Report-Only, see what real browsers would have blocked, and allow a source with one click.
  • Comment Guard keeps comment spam out.
  • Edge WAF Push sends the addresses you block to Cloudflare, so they are refused at the edge.
  • Edge Gateway (optional): the OWASP Core Rule Set in front of your web server, on the same server, with no DNS change. If it stops, traffic goes back to the web server.

Hear about it first, with the fix

  • Vulnerability feed: daily checks of your plugins, themes, core and server software.
  • PHP Advisory Alerts: warn you that a PHP security release is coming, and say whether your server is affected.
  • Certificate Expiry Warning: flags a certificate before it lapses.
  • Alerts by Telegram, email or webhook.
  • Quick Fixes: one-click hardening with undo.
  • Fix Recipes: the exact commands to run, bundled in the plugin and never downloaded, so what you run is what shipped.

Lock down every login

  • 2FA by authenticator app or email, and passkeys with Face ID, Touch ID or Windows Hello. You can make it mandatory for administrators.
  • A hidden login address, lockouts and breached-password checks that never send the password.
  • Emergency Lockdown: one switch for when someone may already be in. It stops new administrators, plugin changes and application password logins, and signs other administrators out.
  • A documented way back in if you are ever locked out, from a wp-config.php safe mode to WP-CLI commands.

Prove your site is clean

  • File Integrity: compares every core and WordPress.org plugin file with the official checksums, with repair and quarantine.
  • Database malware scan looks for malicious code hiding in your database, where a file scan cannot see it.
  • Upgrade Verification: after any change to WordPress, PHP, a theme or a plugin, it checks that the front page, login, REST API and admin still work.
  • Threat Monitor, Persistence Watch, Activity Log and Live Traffic show what is changing and who is knocking.

AI that reviews your site like a penetration tester

  • AI Cyber Audit: reviews your configuration, plugins, users, headers, DNS and TLS, then scores each finding and ranks what to fix first.
  • Deep Dive: adds live checks and AI triage of suspicious plugin code, separating real risks from false alarms.
  • Active Vulnerability Verification (optional, subscription): safe test requests to your own site prove whether a flaw is reachable, and each scan is compared with the last so you can see a fix worked.
  • Use your own Anthropic Claude, Google Gemini or OpenAI key, including Gemini’s free tier, or choose Managed AI and hold no key at all.

Why people choose it

  • Every protection layer is free. Two-factor, passkeys, the firewall, virtual patching and country blocking are not held back for a paid tier.
  • It explains every fix step by step, instead of only raising a warning.
  • It never acts behind your back. Nothing deletes or deactivates a plugin, and fixes are yours to apply and undo.
  • Nothing is sent anywhere on a default install. Every external service stays idle until you turn it on.

What is paid

Only two things, and both are optional. Managed AI is about $10 USD a month through PayPal if you would rather not hold an API key. Active Vulnerability Verification needs the same subscription. Everything else is free.

Developer tools included

  • Code block with syntax highlighting, Mermaid diagrams and charts, all served from your own site.
  • Export to PDF, SMTP Mail, Server Logs, Performance Monitor, and a SQL Query Tool.

External services

Nothing below is contacted on a default install; each service is idle until you configure or click something. API keys are your own, stored in wp_options and sent only to that service, never to CloudScale. Unless an entry says otherwise, no post content, visitor data, database contents, passwords or credentials are sent. A visitor’s page load triggers nothing, except Telegram alerts you set up (failed login, REST authentication failure, CSP report); everything else runs from a scheduled task or an administrator’s action.

Full reference, with every data item and cache time: https://cloudscale.consulting/external-services/

WordPress.org APIs (integrity checks)

Service: WordPress.org, https://wordpress.org
Endpoints: api.wordpress.org/core/checksums/1.0/, /plugins/info/1.0/ and /1.2/; downloads.wordpress.org plugin-checksums/, theme/, and on Repair only release/ and plugin/ zips
Data sent: Your WordPress version and locale, or a plugin or theme’s slug and version.
When: During a File Integrity check, Site Audit scan or Update Risk Assessor run. Off by default.

Privacy: https://wordpress.org/about/privacy/ (no separate terms are published for these APIs)

CloudScale lookups and data lists (optional, off by default)

Service: CloudScale Consulting (plugin author), https://cloudscale.consulting
Endpoints and data sent, all on api.cloudscale.consulting:

  • /whoami: nothing but the plugin’s name and version; the server sees the requesting address, which is the answer. At most daily, only if this site cannot find its own address, after you turn on CVE Alerts (Security tab), or on Check my address.
  • /vuln-lookup and /v1/software-releases: one component per request (a plugin or theme slug, WordPress version, or server product and version), never your hostname, site URL or plugin list. During a scan or host software check you start, and daily once CVE Alerts is on (Security tab).
  • /v1/pwned-range/: the first 5 hex characters of the password’s SHA-1 hash, never the password or full hash. On setting a password, once you choose Warn or Block (Login tab).
  • /v1/php-advisories, /ip-reputation-feed, /v1/virtual-patches and /v1/plugin-models: nothing. Up to hourly once you tick Send PHP advisory alerts; daily or on “Refresh now” once set to Log or Block (Firewall tab); weekly at most once an AI key is saved.

Privacy: https://cloudscale.consulting/privacy/
Terms: https://cloudscale.consulting/terms/

CloudScale Managed AI and Active Verification (optional, paid subscription)

Service: CloudScale Consulting (plugin author), https://cloudscale.consulting
Endpoints: on api.cloudscale.consulting: /v1/messages, /v1/messages-async, /v1/images, /v1/openai-chat, /nuclei-scan, /checkout, /checkout-start, /status, /cancel, /refund-request, /recover, /recover/verify, /contact; /billing-portal and /manage open in your browser, never called by the plugin.
Data sent: AI features: the data listed under Anthropic below, or a post’s title and summary for an image. Billing and Leave us a message: your email address, site URL, message, and any unconfirmed PayPal reference. The PayPal button: product name, hostname and any email you typed. Active Verification: the domain to scan and a scan id; CloudScale’s servers then send real HTTP requests to a site you own, the only active test, and no scanning tool ships with this plugin. Every request carries your licence key, plugin name and version. Never your own API keys.
When: While “Use Managed AI” is on and you run an AI feature; when you click a billing button, Send message, “Run Active Verification” or “Check ownership”; status at most every 10 minutes on the Home tab with a licence key stored.

Privacy: https://cloudscale.consulting/privacy/
Terms: https://cloudscale.consulting/terms/

CloudScale Fix Recipe Usage and Fix Order (optional, opt-in, off by default)

Service: CloudScale Consulting (plugin author), https://cloudscale.consulting
Endpoints: on api.cloudscale.consulting: /remediation-event and /remediation-plan
Data sent: Your licence key and plugin and recipe versions, plus the recipe, button and severity (usage) or failed check identifiers with severity and category, and your WordPress version (fix order). Never your site URL, IP address, file contents or anything you type.
When: Only once you tick “Help CloudScale improve these fix recipes” (Quick Fixes), on opening, copying or downloading a recipe; or “Ask CloudScale what order to fix these in” (Site Audit), after an audit. The reply is an order and warnings, never code.

Privacy: https://cloudscale.consulting/privacy/
Terms: https://cloudscale.consulting/terms/

Cloudflare IP ranges (trusted-proxy list)

Service: Cloudflare, Inc., https://www.cloudflare.com
Endpoint: https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/ips
Data sent: Nothing.
When: Only after you choose Cloudflare under Visitor IP Source: on saving, then weekly. Off by default.

Privacy: https://www.cloudflare.com/privacypolicy/
Terms: https://www.cloudflare.com/website-terms/

Cloudflare API (optional: cache purge, comment rate limit, edge blocking)

Service: Cloudflare, Inc., https://www.cloudflare.com
Endpoints: api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/zones (purge_cache; /rulesets/phases/http_ratelimit/entrypoint, /rulesets/{id}/rules/; /firewall/access_rules/rules)
Data sent: Your API token, plus URLs to invalidate, one rate-limit rule, or blocked IPs.
When: With a zone ID and token: purge on publish or “Purge cache”; daily and on Test; rule changes by button; Edge WAF Push (off by default) every 5 minutes.

Privacy: https://www.cloudflare.com/privacypolicy/
Terms: https://www.cloudflare.com/terms/

OpenStreetMap basemaps (attack-origin map)

Service: OpenStreetMap Foundation, https://www.openstreetmap.org
Endpoint: tile.openstreetmap.org (and its a, b, c subdomains; path zoom/x/y.png)
Data sent: Tile coordinates, plus what a browser sends with any image request (IP address, user agent).
When: Only while an administrator views the map on the Login Security tab, from their browser, never the server. Not bundled: see the FAQ.

Privacy: https://osmfoundation.org/wiki/Privacy_Policy
Terms: https://osmfoundation.org/wiki/Terms_of_Use

Wordfence Intelligence API (optional, your API key)

Service: Defiant, Inc. (Wordfence), https://www.wordfence.com
Endpoint: www.wordfence.com/api/intelligence/v3/vulnerabilities/scanner
Data sent: Nothing about your site; the public dataset is downloaded and matched locally.
When: Only during a security scan with a key entered.

Privacy: https://www.wordfence.com/privacy-policy/
Terms: https://www.wordfence.com/wordfence-intelligence-terms-and-conditions/

Anthropic Claude API (optional, your API key)

Service: Anthropic PBC, https://www.anthropic.com
Endpoint: api.anthropic.com/v1/messages
Data sent: AI audits: site URL; plugin, theme, PHP and server versions; security settings and check results (permissions, headers, SSH, exposed files, table prefix, login and 2FA counts); usernames of administrators with a weak login or no two-factor; for the deep dive, flagged PHP snippets and core-integrity and malware file paths. Site Audit: sample post titles and URLs. Site Optimizer: DB table and column names, a plugin’s changelog, or text you paste. Thumbnails: post title and summary.
When: An AI-labelled button, “Test connection” or a scheduled scan you enabled, with Anthropic selected.

Privacy: https://www.anthropic.com/legal/privacy
Terms: https://www.anthropic.com/legal/commercial-terms

Google Gemini API (optional, your API key)

Service: Google LLC, https://ai.google/
Endpoint: generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta/models/
Data sent: As Anthropic above.
When: As Anthropic above, with Gemini selected.

Privacy: https://policies.google.com/privacy
Terms: https://policies.google.com/terms

OpenAI API (optional, your API key)

Service: OpenAI, LLC, openai.com
Endpoints: api.openai.com/v1/responses and api.openai.com/v1/images/generations
Data sent: Your post title and excerpt, for an image prompt. AI features: as Anthropic above.
When: On “Generate” in the AI Image Generator with ChatGPT as prompt writer, “Test connection”, or AI features with OpenAI selected.

Privacy policy: https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/your-data
Terms of service: openai.com/policies/terms-of-use/

PayPal API (optional, Managed AI checkout)

Service: PayPal Holdings, Inc., https://developer.paypal.com
Endpoints: on api-m.paypal.com (or api-m.sandbox.paypal.com): v1/oauth2/token, v2/checkout/orders, v1/billing/subscriptions/ID; www.paypal.com/sdk/js (browser SDK). Direct API calls only where wp-config.php defines PayPal credentials.
Data sent: Your email address, the amount, a reference and return addresses. The SDK load carries CloudScale’s public client ID.
When: Only when you start or check a PayPal subscription on the Home tab.

Privacy: https://www.paypal.com/us/legalhub/paypal/privacy-full
Terms: https://www.paypal.com/us/legalhub/paypal/useragreement-full

Telegram API (optional, alert notifications)

Service: Telegram Messenger Inc., https://telegram.org
Endpoints: api.telegram.org, Bot API methods sendMessage and getUpdates
Data sent: The alert text and your site URL. Alerts can include PHP error details, the username tried, IP address, country, request path and user agent, scan and performance summaries, and the contact form’s email and message.
When: With your bot token and chat ID set, when an enabled alert fires. “Fetch Chat ID” sends only your token.

Privacy: https://telegram.org/privacy
Terms: https://telegram.org/tos

GitHub / GitLab (optional, GitHub Sync)

Service: GitHub, Inc. and GitLab Inc.
Endpoints: api.github.com and gitlab.com (or your self-hosted GitLab host)
Data sent: Repository owner, name, branch and file path; no token or site data.
When: When an editor links a code block to a file or clicks Sync, and daily for linked blocks.

GitHub Privacy: https://docs.github.com/en/site-policy/privacy-policies/github-general-privacy-statement
Terms: https://docs.github.com/en/site-policy/github-terms/github-terms-of-service
GitLab Privacy: https://about.gitlab.com/privacy/
Terms: https://about.gitlab.com/terms/

DB-IP GeoIP Database (optional, Visitor Map)

Service: DB-IP.com, https://db-ip.com
Endpoint: download.db-ip.com (this month’s dbip-city-lite .mmdb.gz)
Data sent: Only a GET for the file, queried locally; no IP address reaches DB-IP.
When: On “Download / Update GeoIP Database”, then monthly until you untick the refresh.

Privacy: https://db-ip.com/privacy.php
Terms: https://db-ip.com/db/lite.php#faq6

Uptime heartbeat (optional, off by default, your own endpoint)

Endpoint: An https URL you set (Activity tab), your own monitor, not CloudScale.
Data sent: Site URL, timezone, time, a one-time value, your token, plugin version and health signals. No names, emails, paths or IPs.
When: Every 5 minutes once on with a URL and token; while deactivated too if you install the loader.

Your own server addresses (optional, your own endpoint)

Endpoints: Addresses you enter, never CloudScale: the alert webhook URL (Alerts tab), csdt_fpm_probe_url (Diagnostics tab) and csdt_devtools_cf_origin_refresh_url (Thumbnails tab).
Data sent: Signed JSON alerts to the webhook; otherwise a GET, and the origin refresh adds your host name and page path.
When: On an alert or weekly report; when you view FPM status; just before a Cloudflare purge. Nothing while empty.

sections.faq:
Where do Managed AI requests go?

To CloudScale. CloudScale runs them on secure frontier models from various providers, under its own account.

Why does a small site need serious security?

Because attacks are automated. Bots scan every reachable WordPress site, whatever its size, and try new exploits within hours of a flaw being published. Most flaws are in plugins and themes, so a site is only as safe as its least maintained plugin. AI now writes and adapts attacks faster than ever. A hacked site can be blacklisted by search engines, used to send spam or steal visitors’ data, and cleaning it up costs far more than preventing it.

What do you mean by “the layers banks rely on”?

The same kinds of controls a bank puts around its online services, built into WordPress:

  • Strong sign-in: two-factor (authenticator app, email or passkeys), a hidden login address, lockouts and a breached-password check.
  • A web application firewall: 21 rules against SQL injection, cross-site scripting, code execution and more, plus rate limiting, IP reputation and country blocking.
  • Virtual patching: narrow, signed rules that block a published flaw in your installed plugins until you update.
  • Integrity checking: every core and WordPress.org plugin file compared with the official checksums, with repair and quarantine.
  • Browser protection: a Content Security Policy and security headers.
  • Monitoring and response: activity log, threat monitor, alerts and an Emergency Lockdown switch.
  • Optional edge protection: a gateway with the OWASP Core Rule Set in front of the web server.

This describes the controls. It is not a certification.

How does it warn me before an attack?

It watches for the conditions attackers look for, then tells you what to do. The vulnerability feed checks your plugins, themes, core and server software daily once CVE Alerts is on. PHP Advisory Alerts tell you when a PHP security release is coming and whether your server is affected. The Certificate Expiry Warning flags a certificate before it lapses. The audit finds exposed files, weak settings and missing headers. Each finding comes with a fix: a one-click Quick Fix with undo, or a bundled Fix Recipe with the exact commands to run.

How is this different from other security plugins?

  • Every protection layer is free. Two-factor, passkeys, the firewall, virtual patching and country blocking are not held back for a paid tier. Only Managed AI and Active Vulnerability Verification are paid, and both are optional.
  • It tells you what to do, step by step, instead of only raising a warning.
  • It never changes your site behind your back: nothing deletes or deactivates a plugin, and fixes are yours to apply and undo.
  • Nothing is sent anywhere on a default install. AI features use your own key unless you choose Managed AI.

What do the AI defences do?

The AI Cyber Audit reviews your configuration, plugins, users, headers, DNS and TLS the way a penetration tester would, then scores each finding and ranks what to fix first. The Deep Dive adds live checks and AI triage of suspicious plugin code, separating real risks from false alarms. Active Vulnerability Verification (optional, subscription) sends safe test requests to your own site to prove whether a flaw is reachable, and compares each scan with the last so you can see a fix worked.

Why does Own-IP discovery run when CVE Alerts is on?

So the automatic blocker always knows the server’s own public address and never blocks it.

How do I install the Edge Gateway?

Click Pair gateway in the Edge Gateway panel (Request Firewall tab), then run the command it shows as root on your web server. The command downloads the installer from https://api.cloudscale.consulting/edge/install (CloudScale Consulting, this plugin’s author). The plugin itself never calls that address and sends it nothing. The gateway takes the site’s traffic on the same server, with no DNS change, and hands it back to the web server if it stops.

What AI providers are supported?

Anthropic Claude (Sonnet 5 and 5.5, Opus 5 and 5.5, Haiku 4.5 and 5.5), Google Gemini (3.8 Flash, 3.6 Flash, 3.5 Flash Lite and 3.1 Pro Preview) and OpenAI (GPT-6.1 Sol, GPT-6 Astra and GPT-6 Luna). You supply your own API key, no keys are stored anywhere other than your WordPress database (wp_options). A free Gemini tier is available.

What does Live Traffic store?

Nothing until you switch it on (Firewall tab). Then, for each request that reaches WordPress: the time, address, Cloudflare country, method, path without its query string, HTTP status, the first 200 characters of the user agent, and the user ID if signed in. Never the query string, body, cookies or referrer. Rows are kept for 24 hours, at most 20,000, and uninstall drops the table. Pages served from a cache never reach PHP, so they are not shown.

How does the Fake Crawler Check work?

A visitor claiming to be Googlebot, Bingbot, Applebot, YandexBot, Baiduspider or Yahoo Slurp has its address checked with forward-confirmed reverse DNS, through your server’s own resolver. The lookup runs after the response is sent and the result is cached, so no visitor waits. It starts in Log only; Block refuses a proven fake on its next request.

How does virtual patching work?

When a plugin or theme you have installed has a published vulnerability, a virtual patch refuses the one kind of request it needs, for example a non-number in one AJAX action’s id field, until you update. The patches come from a feed signed by CloudScale and checked against a key built into the plugin; each one is drafted from the difference between the vulnerable and the fixed release and approved by a person. A patch is a description, not code: it names an AJAX action, REST route or file inside that component, and one of a fixed set of checks the plugin carries. Only patches for a component installed here at an affected version are used, and each stops applying when you update. Off by default; Log only records matches as vpatch in Recent Matches, Block also refuses them. Signed-in editors are never checked, and the firewall’s exceptions apply.

What is the Out of Band Heartbeat?

An optional signed message, every 5 minutes, from WordPress to an uptime monitor you run (such as a Cloudflare Worker). It stops exactly when WordPress stops, and carries a few signals the monitor can alert on: a new administrator, the firewall switched off, a new must-use plugin, persistence watch changes, the plugin deactivated. The token is stored encrypted. Off by default.

What does Upgrade Verification check?

Every 5 minutes the plugin compares a fingerprint of what the site runs: the WordPress version, the PHP version the web server uses, the active theme and each active plugin with its version. When any of them changes, whether through an update in WordPress, copied files or a rebuilt server image, it waits 2 minutes and checks the front page, the login page, the REST API, admin AJAX, PHP fatals since the change, that each changed part reports its new version, core files against WordPress’s checksums (only while file integrity is on), and that scheduled tasks still run. A failure sends one alert. It is a report only: nothing is rolled back or changed, and the requests go only to your own site. On by default; never runs on a standby copy.

What does Edge WAF Push send to Cloudflare?

Only IP addresses, each as one IP Access Rule on your zone with a note marking it as this site’s. An address qualifies when it is blocked here now and was blocked by hand, is a repeat offender, made a firewall attack in Block mode, or is a proven fake crawler in Block mode; the newest 200. An administrator’s address from the last 30 days, your never-block list, private or reserved ranges, Cloudflare’s own ranges and the site’s own address are never sent. Off by default; switched on it starts in Dry run, which only reads. Rules without this site’s mark are never changed. The token needs Zone > Firewall Services > Edit.

What does Emergency Lockdown do?

One switch (Login Security tab, or the link in an alert) for when someone may already be in. While it is on: no registration, no new administrators or role grants, no plugin or theme install, update, edit, activation or theme switch, no application password or XML-RPC logins, and 3 failed logins refuse an address for 30 minutes. Other administrators are signed out. Two-factor and the hidden login page are untouched, and your own and recent administrator addresses are never refused. Release it in wp-admin. The automatic trigger only reports unless you set it to Enforce.

I’m locked out of my site

Try these in order, and undo each one once you are back in.

  1. Add define( 'CSDT_SAFE_MODE', true ); to wp-config.php. For as long as it is there, IP blocks, Auto-Block, country rules, the firewall, Emergency Lockdown and Comment Guard pause, and wp-login.php answers again. Two-factor is still asked for. Nothing is changed in the database, so removing the line turns everything back on.
  2. From a shell, with WP-CLI: wp csdt login show-url prints the login address, wp csdt firewall unblock <ip> (or --all) lifts blocks, and wp csdt 2fa reset <user> clears one lost authenticator app so that user enrols again. wp csdt support prints the support info, secrets removed.
  3. wp csdt fix rollback <fix> --user=<admin> undoes one Site Audit fix.
  4. define( 'CSDT_LOCKDOWN_DISABLE', true ); in wp-config.php suspends Emergency Lockdown, or wp csdt lockdown release releases it.
  5. Last resort: rename the plugin folder in wp-content/plugins. That switches off every protection, two-factor included, so rename it back as soon as you are in.

How does the deep dive scan avoid HTTP gateway timeouts?

The plugin uses fastcgi_finish_request() to close the browser connection immediately, then continues the scan in the same PHP-FPM worker. A progress bar polls every 3 seconds. This does not depend on WP-Cron.

How do I change the syntax color theme?

Go to Cyber & Devtools > Code Block tab > Code Block Settings panel. Select your preferred theme from the dropdown and click Save.

What languages are supported for code highlighting?

highlight.js with auto-detection. The bundled build registers 37 languages, and accepts 112 names in total once aliases are counted: Bash, Shell, Python, JavaScript, TypeScript, PHP, SQL, Go, Rust, Java, C, C++, C#, Objective-C, Ruby, Swift, Kotlin, Lua, Perl, R, VB.NET, WebAssembly, JSON, YAML, XML, HTML, CSS, SCSS, Less, Markdown, Makefile, Dockerfile, GraphQL, INI/TOML, diff and plain text.

HCL and Terraform are accepted and highlighted with the INI/TOML grammar: highlight.js has no HCL grammar of its own, and rather than ship an unmaintained third-party one we map it to the closest grammar that is bundled, which covers keys, quoted strings, numbers, booleans and comments.

Can the code block draw charts?

Yes. Set the block’s language to Chart (or paste a “`chart fence) and write one setting or series per line, for example type: bar, title: Revenue by quarter, x: Q1, Q2, Q3, then 2025: 12, 15, 17 and 2026: 19, 23, 26. Types are line, area, bar, hbar, stacked, pie and donut. Other settings: subtitle, x-label, y-label, y-min, y-max, prefix, suffix, source, height, colors. A line whose x values are numbers is plotted to scale, and a series may give its own points as 0:400, 5:700. Readers get a legend that hides or shows each series, tooltips, a Source button and the light or dark toggle. A chart with a mistake shows its source and the line that is wrong. The bundled chart library loads only on pages with a chart block.

Can I paste a Chart.js, Vega or Vega-Lite chart?

Yes. A code block whose language is Chart or Chart.js (a chart orchartjs fence) and whose content starts with { is read as a Chart.js configuration in JSON, the type, data and options object that Chart.js documents and that AI assistants write. A block whose language is Vega or Vega-Lite (a vega orvega-lite fence) is drawn from its JSON specification. Colours you set are kept and anything you leave unset follows the block’s light or dark theme. It must be JSON: no functions, comments or trailing commas. A Vega chart may load data files from your own site only, so put the data in the specification as values or upload the file to the media library. Vega expressions are run by Vega’s interpreter rather than eval, so charts draw on sites with a strict Content Security Policy. Each library loads only on pages that use it.

Can the code block draw Mermaid diagrams?

Yes. Set the block’s language to Mermaid diagram (or paste a “`mermaid fence) and the page draws the diagram. A Source button shows the text, Copy copies it, and the theme button redraws it in light or dark. If the diagram has an error, the block shows its source with a one-line reason. The bundled Mermaid library loads only on pages with a Mermaid block, and draws with its strict security level.

Why are the map tiles not bundled with the plugin?

A world basemap is hundreds of megabytes, so it cannot practically ship inside a plugin. The tiles are OpenStreetMap’s own rendering, credited in the map’s attribution control. They are fetched by the administrator’s own browser only while the attack-origin map is on screen, never by the server and never on a visitor’s page load; the full disclosure is under External services above.

What third-party libraries are bundled, and under what licences?

The following open-source libraries are bundled in minified form. Unminified source is available at the linked repositories.

  • highlight.js 11.12.0, syntax highlighting engine. The bundled assets/highlight.min.js is upstream’s own published browser build, unmodified, and assets/hljs-lang-dockerfile.min.js plus the assets/hljs-*.min.css themes are upstream files from the same 11.12.0 release. License: BSD 3-Clause. Source: https://github.com/highlightjs/highlight.js
  • Mermaid 12.2.0, draws diagrams from text in the code block. The bundled assets/mermaid.min.js is upstream’s own published dist/mermaid.min.js, unmodified, with its licence in assets/mermaid.LICENSE.txt. License: MIT. License: DejaVu Fonts License (a permissive, GPL-compatible free licence derived from the Bitstream Vera Fonts License). Source: https://github.com/dejavu-fonts/dejavu-fonts

All licences are GPL-compatible.

Does the plugin add public REST endpoints?

Two, both open by necessity and both limited. csdt/v1/csp-report (POST) receives the violation reports browsers send without credentials; it exists only while CSP violation logging is on, accepts 20 reports per address per 10 minutes, cuts each field to 512 characters and keeps the latest 100. The Custom 404 leaderboard (hiscore/<game>, GET and POST) lets visitors read and post game scores; posting is limited to 5 per address per game per 10 minutes. Edge Gateway routes and the PHP-FPM report route, when in use, also take requests without a login, but only with a valid signature or token. Nothing else is reachable without logging in.

Why does the Performance Monitor’s query list ask me to edit wp-config.php?

WordPress records each query and its timing only while the SAVEQUERIES constant is on, and a plugin may not switch that on for your whole site. Add define( 'SAVEQUERIES', true ); to wp-config.php (the DB tab has a copy button), and remove it when you have finished, because it records every query on every request. Everything else in the monitor works without it.

Is syntax highlighting loaded from a CDN?

No. highlight.js, Mermaid, Chart.js and Vega ship inside the plugin and load from its own /assets/ directory. No CDN request is ever made for syntax highlighting, diagrams or charts.

Outbound admin links (browser navigation only, the plugin sends no data)

Some admin screens contain ordinary hyperlinks you may click; the plugin itself never contacts these sites: ipinfo.io (whois lookup beside logged attacker IPs), documentation and product pages cited in audit findings and help text (gravityforms.com, wpml.org, learndash.com, affiliatewp.com, memberpress.com, paidmembershipspro.com, berocket.com, support.microsoft.com, help.yahoo.com, zoho.com, support.google.com), the pages where you obtain your own API key or manage your own account (console.anthropic.com, aistudio.google.com, platform.openai.com, dash.cloudflare.com), this plugin’s own help site (help.cloudscale.consulting), the public advisory page for a CVE or advisory listed in a scan result (a link the vulnerability lookup returned, or wordfence.com/threat-intel/… for a Wordfence advisory), and social-preview debuggers (facebook.com, linkedin.com, twitter.com). Separately, Social Preview Diagnostics, when you run it, fetches your own pages, your robots.txt and the image each page names in its og:image tag (wherever that image is hosted) the way link-preview crawlers do, sending their published user-agent strings to your own site; those strings contain www.facebook.com and www.linkedin.com, which the plugin never contacts.

How do I allow third-party services in the Content Security Policy?

The policy the plugin builds allows your own site and nothing else. Anything your pages load from elsewhere (analytics, adverts, fonts, embedded video, a payment form) you add yourself in the Allowed sources field, one directive per line, for example script-src analytics.example.com. Start in Report-Only: the Violation Log lists what real browsers would have blocked, and an Allow button beside each entry adds that source for you.

The plugin ships no list of third-party hosts and no service presets. Earlier versions did; a site upgraded from one keeps sending its policy as Report-Only until the panel is saved once, so nothing that used to be allowed is suddenly blocked.

What is CloudScale Managed AI, and do I need it?

No, every AI feature works with your own Anthropic, Google Gemini or OpenAI key, which you supply and pay for directly. Managed AI is the alternative for people who would rather not hold an API key at all: about $10 USD a month via PayPal.

One allowance, three capabilities: 200 text requests, 30 generated images and 500,000 characters of narration each month. Demanding work runs on CS-Text-Pro and everyday work on CS-Text-1.

It does not lock you in. If the managed service is ever unavailable, the plugin falls back to your own key automatically, so keeping a key configured is worth doing either way. The same subscription also powers the CloudScale SEO plugin. Card details are entered on PayPal’s hosted checkout and never reach this plugin, and your own API keys are never sent to CloudScale.

Tiers are named by capability (CS-Text-1, CS-Text-Pro, CS-Voice-1, CS-Voice-Pro, CS-Image-1) because which engine serves a tier is chosen per job and changes as better or cheaper options appear.

Can Active Vulnerability Verification scan a site other than mine?

No. It only ever scans the site your CloudScale license is registered to, there is no field for a different target. To audit another domain, that site needs its own license.

The scan is rate-limited per license and has a hard time limit per run.

Why do the fix commands ship inside the plugin instead of being downloaded?

Because they are shell commands you may run as root. Fetching them over the network would mean a compromised or impersonated server could hand your server arbitrary commands to run with full privileges. The recipes are bundled in the plugin and are never downloaded, so what you see is what shipped, reviewed, in the version you installed.

Does the plugin check my own site in the background?

Not unless you switch it on. The Exposed folders check is off by default: until you tick “Exposed folders check” in the AI Cyber Audit panel it makes no requests and schedules nothing.

Switched on, once a day it asks this site, and only this site, for the real folders on its own server, for the files whose content proves a leak (a .git folder, a copy of wp-config.php, a .env file, a backup, a database tool) and for about 1,500 common leftover, backup and staging folder names, in small batches. It contacts no outside service, has no target field and cannot be pointed at any site but its own. The result is kept in your own database for the site audit to read.

A name only becomes a finding when the content of the answer proves it, such as a real file listing or a real git file. A page that merely answers 200 is not a finding. The check sees the site as its own server reaches it; a proxy in front of the site may be stricter. Unticking the box stops the daily run and removes the stored result.

The Certificate Expiry Warning (Activity tab) is off by default too. Switched on, once a day it opens a secure connection to this site’s host name and to up to 10 other host names you list, reads the certificate each one presents and closes the connection. No page is requested and nothing about your site is sent. It contacts no CloudScale or third-party service, only the names you entered, and refuses one that points at a private address.

Does the plugin tell me about PHP security releases?

Yes. PHP Advisory Alerts (Security tab, beside Host Software) sends one alert each when php.net announces an upcoming security release (with the release time in your timezone and in UTC), when the release for your PHP branch is out (saying whether this site is affected), when your branch is end of life and will not get the fix, and when this site runs the fixed version. The version checked is the one your web server runs, read on an admin page load, never the command line PHP. Alerts go to Telegram, if set up, and the admin email address. It changes nothing on your site, and the dashboard widget shows the current state. Off by default: tick Send PHP advisory alerts to start it.

Does the plugin hide the WordPress version?

Only if you ask it to. “Hide WP Version” is off by default. Switched on, the plugin removes the generator tag that WordPress prints in the page head and the version numbers on script and style links. Switch it off and WordPress prints them again.

Does the plugin ever change or remove anything without being told to?

Nothing runs on a schedule that alters your site, and the plugin never executes a shell command: the fix recipes above are text for you to run yourself. Two presentation defaults apply from activation, each with its own switch in the admin: WordPress’s emoji image script is skipped so emoji render natively, and each post shows an Export to PDF button. The custom 404 page and the performance monitor are both off until you switch them on, so a new install leaves your theme’s 404 template and your admin requests exactly as they were.

No Quick Fix deletes or deactivates another plugin. “List inactive plugins”, offered by the site audit when it finds deactivated plugins still on disk, is read-only: it names each one with its version so you can review them and remove any you no longer need from Plugins, Installed Plugins yourself. The plugin does not edit wp-config.php either: the “Limit to 5 Revisions” fix applies its cap at runtime, and can be undone.

  • IMPROVED: the Cloudflare API token is stored encrypted and the Credentials panel shows only whether it is set.

1.10.1061

  • IMPROVED: the Site Audit and the weekly security report now include PHP security advisories: critical when a PHP security release is announced or out and this site is not on the fixed version, high when the PHP branch is end of life, with the release time in your timezone and UTC and a link to PHP Advisory Alerts. Read from stored data only, so it works with the alerts off and contacts nothing.
  • FIXED: Upgrade Verification no longer skips its PHP fatals check where PHP logs to the container’s output (Docker). The plugin records each fatal page load itself, so the check counts fatals with or without a readable log.

1.10.1060

  • IMPROVED: the Activity Log has a search box (user, IP, event and detail, across every page) that combines with the event filter and carries into Export CSV; its settings and toolbar now line up. “Where to fix this” opens, scrolls to and highlights the exact panel, and each finding names the same place. Tab introductions are a card aligned with the panels, with the tip on its own line. Audit findings that name posts link to each post’s view and edit screens.

1.10.1059

  • NEW: Upgrade Verification panel (Activity tab). After core, PHP, the theme or a plugin changes (including file copies and image rebuilds), checks the front page, login, REST API, admin AJAX, new PHP fatals, that each change landed whole, core checksums and the schedule, and alerts on a failure. Report only, contacts only your own site. On by default.

1.10.1057

  • NEW: Out of Band Heartbeat panel (Activity tab). The uptime heartbeat is now signed (HMAC with a timestamp and one-time value, so it cannot be replayed), carries signals your monitor can alert on, stores its token encrypted, and can keep beating from a must-use loader while the plugin is deactivated. Off by default; existing heartbeat settings carry over.

1.10.1056

  • NEW: PHP Advisory Alerts. One alert each when php.net announces a PHP security release, when the fix for your branch is out (affected or not, and what to do), when your branch is end of life, and when this site runs the fix. Uses the web server’s PHP, never the command line’s; times in your timezone and UTC. Off by default; alerts only.

1.10.1055

  • NEW: Virtual Patching (Firewall tab). A signed feed of narrow per-CVE rules, applied only to a plugin or theme installed here at an affected version, each lifting itself once you update. Off by default; Log only records matches as vpatch in Recent Matches, Block refuses them.

1.10.1054

  • FIXED: the Fake Crawler Check no longer raises a PHP error at the end of a request that claims to be a search engine crawler, so its verdict is now stored.

1.10.1053

  • NEW: Firewall rule exceptions. Lift one rule on one path, optionally for one parameter only, instead of switching it off for the whole site. The Except button on a Recent Matches row fills in the line. A path containing .. or // never gets an exception.
  • NEW: Fake Crawler Check. A visitor claiming to be Googlebot, Bingbot, Applebot, YandexBot, Baiduspider or Yahoo Slurp is checked with forward-confirmed reverse DNS after the response is sent, and the verdict is cached. Log only by default; Block is refused while every claim has failed, which means the site is reading a proxy’s address.
  • NEW: Live Traffic, a feed of the requests that reach WordPress, with filters, pause and auto-refresh. Off by default. Never stores the query string, body, cookies or referrer; kept 24 hours, at most 20,000 rows.

1.10.1048

  • NEW: Export to PDF. Every post has a button, for every visitor, that saves the article as a PDF through the browser’s own Save as PDF, so the text stays selectable and the links work. Only the article prints, without the menu, sidebar, ads or comment form, whatever the theme. Headings stay with the text they introduce, and images, tables, code blocks and diagrams that fit on a page are never split; a wide diagram shrinks to the page instead of being cut off. Nothing is generated on the server or sent anywhere. On by default; switch it off under Code Block Settings.

1.10.1046

  • Changed: every security report (AI audit, deep dive, Site Audit) opens with an executive summary: a verdict, a score gauge, findings by severity, what to fix first and what is already good. Each severity has its own colour, heading and timeframe, and colours now print.
  • Changed: the deep dive merges a finding that both halves report into one.
  • Fixed: the cron audit no longer reports this plugin’s own scheduled tasks as belonging to no active plugin.
  • Fixed: country flags are built without mb_chr(), which WordPress 7.1 polyfills.
  • Changed: the AI model list class is renamed CSDT_Model_Feed, under the plugin’s own prefix.
  • Fixed: the weekly AI model-list request now sends a fixed User-Agent instead of WordPress’s default, which carries the site URL, so it sends nothing, as documented. Site Audit and Social Preview requests to your own site name the plugin too.
  • Changed: the remember-me tick box is reworded in every language when the Website field is removed.

1.10.1027

  • Changed: alert settings (Telegram, environment label, mute) are stored under this plugin’s own prefix, migrated automatically, and kept in sync with the other CloudScale plugins.

1.10.1023

  • Added: the Other Alerts Show button on the dashboard widget flashes when there is an alert you have not opened yet.

1.10.1022

  • Added: Other Alerts on the dashboard widget folds behind a Show / Hide button, the same as Recent Security Events.

1.10.1020

  • Fixed: the Telegram Alert Log banner no longer reports old delivery failures as a present fault. It shows red only when the newest alert failed, and otherwise says delivery is working and when the last failure was.
  • Fixed: the Telegram Alert Log is readable on a phone. Each message now sits on its own full-width row.

1.10.1019

  • Changed: while Comment Guard refuses links, the comment form’s remember-me tick box says “Save my name and email in this browser” and no longer mentions a website.

1.10.1018

  • Changed: in the weekly security report, low risk exposed files (the WordPress readme and licence file, a leftover folder) are listed and marked low risk, and no longer count as items that need attention.

1.10.1017

  • Added: the weekly security report has an Exposed folders section. It lists each folder or file the Exposed folders check found served to visitors who are not signed in, and counts them as items that need attention. When the check is off or has not finished, it says so.
  • Changed: the message a visitor sees when a comment is refused for containing a link now says first that the comment was not posted, then why, then what to do.

1.10.1016

  • Changed: Auto for Anthropic now uses the newest Claude models: Sonnet 5.5 for standard scans, Opus 5.5 for deep scans and Haiku 5.5 for triage. The older models stay in the list if you prefer them.

1.10.1015

  • Changed: the External services section now lists what the Site Audit sends to your chosen AI provider (sample post titles and URLs, inactive themes, unwritable file paths, exposed folders). Two admin notes that named only Anthropic and Gemini now name OpenAI too.

1.10.1014

  • Fixed: a JavaScript error inside another plugin’s script is sent as a critical alert again. 1.10.1012 turned all of them into warnings. Only one known harmless error, Akismet’s link preview on the Comments screen, is listed as a warning.

Entries before 1.10.1014 are kept in the author’s development changelog.

short_description: The security layers banks rely on, free: firewall, virtual patches, passkeys, integrity checks and AI audits that warn you before attackers strike.
description:
Attackers do not choose targets. Automated scanners probe every WordPress site for flaws published hours earlier. CloudScale Cyber & DevTools puts the layers banks rely on in front of your site, free. It stops the attack, tells you in plain language what is wrong, and gives you the exact steps to fix it.

Why your site needs this now

  • Most WordPress vulnerabilities are in plugins and themes, so a site is only as safe as its least maintained plugin.
  • New exploits arrive within hours of a flaw being published, and AI makes them cheaper and faster to write. Your defence uses AI too.
  • A hacked site can be blacklisted by search engines, used to send spam or used to steal visitors’ data. Cleaning up costs far more than preventing it.

Stop attacks before they do damage

  • Request Firewall: 21 rules against SQL injection, cross-site scripting and code execution, before WordPress handles requests.
  • Virtual Patching: narrow, signed rules that block a published flaw in a plugin or theme you have installed until you update. Each patch is approved by a person, and is a description, never code.
  • CVE Shields: close a vulnerable plugin’s anonymous endpoints until the fixed version is installed, then lift themselves.
  • IP Reputation, Rate Limiting and Country Blocking shut out known bad traffic and floods.
  • Fake Crawler Check: proves that a visitor claiming to be Googlebot or Bingbot really is, with no delay for visitors.
  • Content Security Policy: start in Report-Only, see what real browsers would have blocked, and allow a source with one click.
  • Comment Guard keeps comment spam out.
  • Edge WAF Push sends the addresses you block to Cloudflare, so they are refused at the edge.
  • Edge Gateway (optional): the OWASP Core Rule Set in front of your web server, on the same server, with no DNS change. If it stops, traffic goes back to the web server.

Hear about it first, with the fix

  • Vulnerability feed: daily checks of your plugins, themes, core and server software.
  • PHP Advisory Alerts: warn you that a PHP security release is coming, and say whether your server is affected.
  • Certificate Expiry Warning: flags a certificate before it lapses.
  • Alerts by Telegram, email or webhook.
  • Quick Fixes: one-click hardening with undo.
  • Fix Recipes: the exact commands to run, bundled in the plugin and never downloaded, so what you run is what shipped.

Lock down every login

  • 2FA by authenticator app or email, and passkeys with Face ID, Touch ID or Windows Hello. You can make it mandatory for administrators.
  • A hidden login address, lockouts and breached-password checks that never send the password.
  • Emergency Lockdown: one switch for when someone may already be in. It stops new administrators, plugin changes and application password logins, and signs other administrators out.
  • A documented way back in if you are ever locked out, from a wp-config.php safe mode to WP-CLI commands.

Prove your site is clean

  • File Integrity: compares every core and WordPress.org plugin file with the official checksums, with repair and quarantine.
  • Database malware scan looks for malicious code hiding in your database, where a file scan cannot see it.
  • Upgrade Verification: after any change to WordPress, PHP, a theme or a plugin, it checks that the front page, login, REST API and admin still work.
  • Threat Monitor, Persistence Watch, Activity Log and Live Traffic show what is changing and who is knocking.

AI that reviews your site like a penetration tester

  • AI Cyber Audit: reviews your configuration, plugins, users, headers, DNS and TLS, then scores each finding and ranks what to fix first.
  • Deep Dive: adds live checks and AI triage of suspicious plugin code, separating real risks from false alarms.
  • Active Vulnerability Verification (optional, subscription): safe test requests to your own site prove whether a flaw is reachable, and each scan is compared with the last so you can see a fix worked.
  • Use your own Anthropic Claude, Google Gemini or OpenAI key, including Gemini’s free tier, or choose Managed AI and hold no key at all.

Why people choose it

  • Every protection layer is free. Two-factor, passkeys, the firewall, virtual patching and country blocking are not held back for a paid tier.
  • It explains every fix step by step, instead of only raising a warning.
  • It never acts behind your back. Nothing deletes or deactivates a plugin, and fixes are yours to apply and undo.
  • Nothing is sent anywhere on a default install. Every external service stays idle until you turn it on.

What is paid

Only two things, and both are optional. Managed AI is about $10 USD a month through PayPal if you would rather not hold an API key. Active Vulnerability Verification needs the same subscription. Everything else is free.

Developer tools included

  • Code block with syntax highlighting, Mermaid diagrams and charts, all served from your own site.
  • Export to PDF, SMTP Mail, Server Logs, Performance Monitor, and a SQL Query Tool.

External services

Nothing below is contacted on a default install; each service is idle until you configure or click something. API keys are your own, stored in wp_options and sent only to that service, never to CloudScale. Unless an entry says otherwise, no post content, visitor data, database contents, passwords or credentials are sent. A visitor’s page load triggers nothing, except Telegram alerts you set up (failed login, REST authentication failure, CSP report); everything else runs from a scheduled task or an administrator’s action.

Full reference, with every data item and cache time: https://cloudscale.consulting/external-services/

WordPress.org APIs (integrity checks)

Service: WordPress.org, https://wordpress.org
Endpoints: api.wordpress.org/core/checksums/1.0/, /plugins/info/1.0/ and /1.2/; downloads.wordpress.org plugin-checksums/, theme/, and on Repair only release/ and plugin/ zips
Data sent: Your WordPress version and locale, or a plugin or theme’s slug and version.
When: During a File Integrity check, Site Audit scan or Update Risk Assessor run. Off by default.

Privacy: https://wordpress.org/about/privacy/ (no separate terms are published for these APIs)

CloudScale lookups and data lists (optional, off by default)

Service: CloudScale Consulting (plugin author), https://cloudscale.consulting
Endpoints and data sent, all on api.cloudscale.consulting:

  • /whoami: nothing but the plugin’s name and version; the server sees the requesting address, which is the answer. At most daily, only if this site cannot find its own address, after you turn on CVE Alerts (Security tab), or on Check my address.
  • /vuln-lookup and /v1/software-releases: one component per request (a plugin or theme slug, WordPress version, or server product and version), never your hostname, site URL or plugin list. During a scan or host software check you start, and daily once CVE Alerts is on (Security tab).
  • /v1/pwned-range/: the first 5 hex characters of the password’s SHA-1 hash, never the password or full hash. On setting a password, once you choose Warn or Block (Login tab).
  • /v1/php-advisories, /ip-reputation-feed, /v1/virtual-patches and /v1/plugin-models: nothing. Up to hourly once you tick Send PHP advisory alerts; daily or on “Refresh now” once set to Log or Block (Firewall tab); weekly at most once an AI key is saved.

Privacy: https://cloudscale.consulting/privacy/
Terms: https://cloudscale.consulting/terms/

CloudScale Managed AI and Active Verification (optional, paid subscription)

Service: CloudScale Consulting (plugin author), https://cloudscale.consulting
Endpoints: on api.cloudscale.consulting: /v1/messages, /v1/messages-async, /v1/images, /v1/openai-chat, /nuclei-scan, /checkout, /checkout-start, /status, /cancel, /refund-request, /recover, /recover/verify, /contact; /billing-portal and /manage open in your browser, never called by the plugin.
Data sent: AI features: the data listed under Anthropic below, or a post’s title and summary for an image. Billing and Leave us a message: your email address, site URL, message, and any unconfirmed PayPal reference. The PayPal button: product name, hostname and any email you typed. Active Verification: the domain to scan and a scan id; CloudScale’s servers then send real HTTP requests to a site you own, the only active test, and no scanning tool ships with this plugin. Every request carries your licence key, plugin name and version. Never your own API keys.
When: While “Use Managed AI” is on and you run an AI feature; when you click a billing button, Send message, “Run Active Verification” or “Check ownership”; status at most every 10 minutes on the Home tab with a licence key stored.

Privacy: https://cloudscale.consulting/privacy/
Terms: https://cloudscale.consulting/terms/

CloudScale Fix Recipe Usage and Fix Order (optional, opt-in, off by default)

Service: CloudScale Consulting (plugin author), https://cloudscale.consulting
Endpoints: on api.cloudscale.consulting: /remediation-event and /remediation-plan
Data sent: Your licence key and plugin and recipe versions, plus the recipe, button and severity (usage) or failed check identifiers with severity and category, and your WordPress version (fix order). Never your site URL, IP address, file contents or anything you type.
When: Only once you tick “Help CloudScale improve these fix recipes” (Quick Fixes), on opening, copying or downloading a recipe; or “Ask CloudScale what order to fix these in” (Site Audit), after an audit. The reply is an order and warnings, never code.

Privacy: https://cloudscale.consulting/privacy/
Terms: https://cloudscale.consulting/terms/

Cloudflare IP ranges (trusted-proxy list)

Service: Cloudflare, Inc., https://www.cloudflare.com
Endpoint: https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/ips
Data sent: Nothing.
When: Only after you choose Cloudflare under Visitor IP Source: on saving, then weekly. Off by default.

Privacy: https://www.cloudflare.com/privacypolicy/
Terms: https://www.cloudflare.com/website-terms/

Cloudflare API (optional: cache purge, comment rate limit, edge blocking)

Service: Cloudflare, Inc., https://www.cloudflare.com
Endpoints: api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/zones (purge_cache; /rulesets/phases/http_ratelimit/entrypoint, /rulesets/{id}/rules/; /firewall/access_rules/rules)
Data sent: Your API token, plus URLs to invalidate, one rate-limit rule, or blocked IPs.
When: With a zone ID and token: purge on publish or “Purge cache”; daily and on Test; rule changes by button; Edge WAF Push (off by default) every 5 minutes.

Privacy: https://www.cloudflare.com/privacypolicy/
Terms: https://www.cloudflare.com/terms/

OpenStreetMap basemaps (attack-origin map)

Service: OpenStreetMap Foundation, https://www.openstreetmap.org
Endpoint: tile.openstreetmap.org (and its a, b, c subdomains; path zoom/x/y.png)
Data sent: Tile coordinates, plus what a browser sends with any image request (IP address, user agent).
When: Only while an administrator views the map on the Login Security tab, from their browser, never the server. Not bundled: see the FAQ.

Privacy: https://osmfoundation.org/wiki/Privacy_Policy
Terms: https://osmfoundation.org/wiki/Terms_of_Use

Wordfence Intelligence API (optional, your API key)

Service: Defiant, Inc. (Wordfence), https://www.wordfence.com
Endpoint: www.wordfence.com/api/intelligence/v3/vulnerabilities/scanner
Data sent: Nothing about your site; the public dataset is downloaded and matched locally.
When: Only during a security scan with a key entered.

Privacy: https://www.wordfence.com/privacy-policy/
Terms: https://www.wordfence.com/wordfence-intelligence-terms-and-conditions/

Anthropic Claude API (optional, your API key)

Service: Anthropic PBC, https://www.anthropic.com
Endpoint: api.anthropic.com/v1/messages
Data sent: AI audits: site URL; plugin, theme, PHP and server versions; security settings and check results (permissions, headers, SSH, exposed files, table prefix, login and 2FA counts); usernames of administrators with a weak login or no two-factor; for the deep dive, flagged PHP snippets and core-integrity and malware file paths. Site Audit: sample post titles and URLs. Site Optimizer: DB table and column names, a plugin’s changelog, or text you paste. Thumbnails: post title and summary.
When: An AI-labelled button, “Test connection” or a scheduled scan you enabled, with Anthropic selected.

Privacy: https://www.anthropic.com/legal/privacy
Terms: https://www.anthropic.com/legal/commercial-terms

Google Gemini API (optional, your API key)

Service: Google LLC, https://ai.google/
Endpoint: generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta/models/
Data sent: As Anthropic above.
When: As Anthropic above, with Gemini selected.

Privacy: https://policies.google.com/privacy
Terms: https://policies.google.com/terms

OpenAI API (optional, your API key)

Service: OpenAI, LLC, openai.com
Endpoints: api.openai.com/v1/responses and api.openai.com/v1/images/generations
Data sent: Your post title and excerpt, for an image prompt. AI features: as Anthropic above.
When: On “Generate” in the AI Image Generator with ChatGPT as prompt writer, “Test connection”, or AI features with OpenAI selected.

Privacy policy: https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/your-data
Terms of service: openai.com/policies/terms-of-use/

PayPal API (optional, Managed AI checkout)

Service: PayPal Holdings, Inc., https://developer.paypal.com
Endpoints: on api-m.paypal.com (or api-m.sandbox.paypal.com): v1/oauth2/token, v2/checkout/orders, v1/billing/subscriptions/ID; www.paypal.com/sdk/js (browser SDK). Direct API calls only where wp-config.php defines PayPal credentials.
Data sent: Your email address, the amount, a reference and return addresses. The SDK load carries CloudScale’s public client ID.
When: Only when you start or check a PayPal subscription on the Home tab.

Privacy: https://www.paypal.com/us/legalhub/paypal/privacy-full
Terms: https://www.paypal.com/us/legalhub/paypal/useragreement-full

Telegram API (optional, alert notifications)

Service: Telegram Messenger Inc., https://telegram.org
Endpoints: api.telegram.org, Bot API methods sendMessage and getUpdates
Data sent: The alert text and your site URL. Alerts can include PHP error details, the username tried, IP address, country, request path and user agent, scan and performance summaries, and the contact form’s email and message.
When: With your bot token and chat ID set, when an enabled alert fires. “Fetch Chat ID” sends only your token.

Privacy: https://telegram.org/privacy
Terms: https://telegram.org/tos

GitHub / GitLab (optional, GitHub Sync)

Service: GitHub, Inc. and GitLab Inc.
Endpoints: api.github.com and gitlab.com (or your self-hosted GitLab host)
Data sent: Repository owner, name, branch and file path; no token or site data.
When: When an editor links a code block to a file or clicks Sync, and daily for linked blocks.

GitHub Privacy: https://docs.github.com/en/site-policy/privacy-policies/github-general-privacy-statement
Terms: https://docs.github.com/en/site-policy/github-terms/github-terms-of-service
GitLab Privacy: https://about.gitlab.com/privacy/
Terms: https://about.gitlab.com/terms/

DB-IP GeoIP Database (optional, Visitor Map)

Service: DB-IP.com, https://db-ip.com
Endpoint: download.db-ip.com (this month’s dbip-city-lite .mmdb.gz)
Data sent: Only a GET for the file, queried locally; no IP address reaches DB-IP.
When: On “Download / Update GeoIP Database”, then monthly until you untick the refresh.

Privacy: https://db-ip.com/privacy.php
Terms: https://db-ip.com/db/lite.php#faq6

Uptime heartbeat (optional, off by default, your own endpoint)

Endpoint: An https URL you set (Activity tab), your own monitor, not CloudScale.
Data sent: Site URL, timezone, time, a one-time value, your token, plugin version and health signals. No names, emails, paths or IPs.
When: Every 5 minutes once on with a URL and token; while deactivated too if you install the loader.

Your own server addresses (optional, your own endpoint)

Endpoints: Addresses you enter, never CloudScale: the alert webhook URL (Alerts tab), csdt_fpm_probe_url (Diagnostics tab) and csdt_devtools_cf_origin_refresh_url (Thumbnails tab).
Data sent: Signed JSON alerts to the webhook; otherwise a GET, and the origin refresh adds your host name and page path.
When: On an alert or weekly report; when you view FPM status; just before a Cloudflare purge. Nothing while empty.
